title: Pharmacy Intern
description:
You’ve invested a lot of time and energy in your education. Now you want the chance to make your mark. We offer challenging opportunities for you to learn and grow professionally. In our programs, you’ll be immersed in a culture of continuous improvement, with the goal of changing health care for the better.

Position Summary:

At CVS Health, we are focused on transforming health care for our customers and making our company a great place to work. We help people navigate the health care system – and their personal health care – by improving access, lowering costs and being a trusted partner for every meaningful moment of health. Within our Retail locations, we bring this promise to life with heart every day. Our 3rd year Pharmacy Interns play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise, while developing their own skills in preparation for increasing responsibility.

As a 3rd year Pharmacy Intern, you will be focused on applying didactic learning from pharmacy school into real-world practice to become ready for a Pharmacist role. Under the direction of your preceptor, you will complete a comprehensive training roadmap designed to show you first-hand what it’s like to be part of a pharmacy team while gaining an overview of store, district, and regional operations. You will gain valuable hands-on experience through a training roadmap that includes a combination of Key Learning Experiences (KLEs), activities, and time spent with leaders in your district. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate empathy and genuine care, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.

3rd year Pharmacy Interns are responsible for completion of a comprehensive training roadmap, focusing on KLEs that build aptitude in the following areas. As tenure increases, 3rd year Pharmacy Interns take on increasing responsibility of the safety and effectiveness of operations in the pharmacy, including but not limited to:

  • Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health
  • Following pharmacy workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment
  • Contributing to positive patient experiences showing empathy and genuine care: creating heartfelt and personalized moments while serving patients at pick-up, drive-thru, and over the phone; keeping patients healthy by offering immunizations and other services at the register and over the phone; and demonstrating compassionate care by solving or escalating patient problems
  • Offering to counsel, fielding medical questions, and soliciting information on a patient’s medical history to provide optimal care, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist
  • Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation
  • Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices
  • Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.
  • Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients
  • Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business
  • Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. Complying with CVS policies and procedures to ensure patient safety, compliance with controlled substance dispensing and recordkeeping, and to protect patient privacy and security
  • Delivering additional patient health care services (e.g., immunizations, point-of-care testing, and voluntarily staffing offsite clinics), where allowable by law and supported by required training and certification

Where permissible, the 3rd year Pharmacy Intern may also support immunizations, which includes the following responsibilities:

  • Completing additional licensure and training requirements, in compliance with state Board of Pharmacy regulations, to obtain Technician Immunizer status to support preparing and administering vaccines
  • Educating patients about the importance of vaccines and referring patients to the Pharmacist-on-duty for vaccination questions
  • Monitoring for, and responding to, adverse reactions; reporting adverse reaction events per public health requirements
  • Reviewing and collecting patient information; tracking and documenting for each applicable patient

Required Qualifications:

  • Accepted into, or actively enrolled in, an ACPE accredited college or school of pharmacy
  • Must possess, or be in the process of obtaining, valid intern and/or technician licensure as required

Essential Functions:

  • Regular and predictable attendance, including nights and weekends
  • Ability to complete required training within designated timeframe
  • Attention and Focus:
    • Ability to concentrate on a task over a period of time
    • Ability to pivot quickly from one task to another to meet patient and business needs
    • Ability to confirm prescription information and label accuracy, ensuring patient safety
  • Customer Service and Team Orientation:
    • Actively look for ways to help people, and do so in a friendly manner
    • Notice and understand patients’ reactions, and respond appropriately
  • Communication Skills:
    • Use and understand verbal and written communication to interact with patients and colleagues

title: Networking Managed Services Engineer (L2)
description:
Make an impact with NTT DATA
Join a company that is pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We are renowned for our technical excellence and leading innovations, and for making a difference to our clients and society. Our workplace embraces diversity and inclusion – it’s a place where you can grow, belong and thrive.

Your day at NTT DATA
As a Networking Managed Services Engineer (L2) at NTT DATA, you'll take on a developing engineering role where your main goal is to ensure our clients' IT infrastructure and systems remain operational. You'll achieve this by proactively monitoring, identifying, investigating, and resolving technical incidents and problems. You'll work closely with our clients and internal teams to ensure that services are restored swiftly, in line with our service level agreements (SLAs).

Your day will revolve around reviewing client requests and tickets, applying your technical expertise to resolve them efficiently and effectively. You'll be the go-to person for second-line support, handling incidents and requests of medium complexity. In addition to your daily tasks, you'll have opportunities to contribute to exciting project work from time to time.

You'll proactively monitor work queues, execute operational tasks, and update tickets with the actions you've taken. Identifying, analysing, and logging issues before they escalate will be a key part of your role. You'll communicate with other teams and clients to provide support and ensure that changes are executed with clear risk identification and mitigation plans.

As part of the shift handover process, you'll highlight key tickets and upcoming critical tasks for the next shift. When needed, you'll escalate tickets to ensure the right focus from our Centres of Excellence (CoE) and other teams. Collaborating with our automation teams, you'll work on optimizing efforts and automating routine tasks, all while coaching our Service desk and L1 teams in both technical and behavioural skills.

You'll also establish monitoring for client infrastructure, leading and managing initial client escalations for operational issues. Contributing to the change management process, you'll log change requests, execute approved maintenance activities, and audit incident and request tickets for quality. Your insights will drive trend analysis reports, identifying tasks suitable for automation to reduce tickets and optimize efforts. You might also support disaster recovery functions and other related tasks as needed.

To thrive in this role, you need to have:
  • Proficiency in technologies such as Pulse Secure SSL VPN, Palo Alto, Fortinet, Cisco Nexus switches/routers/firewalls, and more familiarity with ticketing tools.

The team is responsible for the end-to-end development and Confidential - Default realization of new product propositions with the goal of driving business growth by bringing existing, differentiating and new product propositions to market. You’ll be reporting to the Functional Group Lead Software Development and will be working within a team of highly motivated developers, and you will be based in our Shenzhen site.

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Electronics or a related field; a Master’s degree is a plus.

• At least 8 years of software development experience, including 3 or more years in a technical leadership role such as lead developer, software designer or architect for embedded, connected or IoT products.

• Strong knowledge of object-oriented design, design patterns and refactoring; Experience in scripting and engineering automation is a plus.

• Strong embedded software expertise in C/C++, with practical experience in RTOS and/or embedded Linux and in developing Wi-Fi- and Bluetooth Low Energy-enabled devices using relevant SoCs, modules and IoT SDKs. Experience with real-time audio or video technologies, such as WebRTC, RTSP, is a plus.

• Experience in IoT security and privacy, including secure provisioning, device identity, PKI, certificate management and TLS, together with knowledge of applicable cybersecurity standards and regulations. Experience with regulated product development, including IEC 62304 and relevant FDA guidance for medical devices, is a plus.

• Strong knowledge of software development lifecycles, architecture governance, integration and verification practices; experience applying both V-model and Agile approaches is required. • Experience working with ODM/JDM partners in Greater China region, to ensure the quality, security and regulatory compliance of outsourced design and implementation.

• Ability to align product owners, system architects, embedded, mobile and cloud teams, and external partners on requirements, interfaces and technical trade-o s.

• Experience in technical planning, estimation and risk management, with the ability to coach engineers and communicate effectively across functions, cultures and organizational levels.

• Customer Focus

We are looking for an experienced SAP Basis Administrator to support SAP ABAP, database, operating system, and virtual infrastructure environments. The role combines SAP Basis operations, technical troubleshooting, database activities, server administration, and cloud and virtualization support. You will work with international teams, including colleagues in China and other SAP delivery locations.

This position follows a two-shift schedule covering 08:00–16:00 and 16:00–00:00 CET. Candidates must be willing and able to work according to the agreed shift rotation.

  • Monitor system availability, stability, capacity, and performance.

  • Investigate SAP system errors and identify appropriate corrective actions.
  • Support SAP license updates and related administration activities.

  • Apply pragmatic troubleshooting methods to resolve operational issues efficiently.

  • Participate in technical discussions, handovers, and troubleshooting sessions across locations and time zones.
  • Communicate technical status, service impact, and resolution progress clearly.
  • Collaborate effectively with internal teams, SAP representatives, and customer stakeholders.

  • Hands-on SAP Basis administration and operational support experience.
  • Experience performing SAP ABAP system health and performance checks.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills and experience analyzing SAP system logs and developer traces.
  • Operational knowledge of SAP HANA, SAP MaxDB, and SAP ASE/Sybase databases.
  • Experience starting and stopping SAP application and database systems.
  • Knowledge of SAP license administration and database log and data maintenance.
  • Basic knowledge of SAP Fiori and non-ABAP systems.
  • Intermediate knowledge of Windows Server and SUSE Linux Enterprise Server.
  • Intermediate VMware knowledge, preferably including VMware Cloud Director and vApp administration.
  • Ability to understand and respond to German-language customer tickets, including with the support of translation tools.
  • Basic knowledge of Google Cloud Platform.
  • Experience working with ServiceNow or a comparable ITSM platform.
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Office 365.
  • Pragmatic working style and strong problem-solving capabilities.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively in international and geographically distributed teams.
  • Willingness and flexibility to work in shifts covering 08:00–16:00 and 16:00–00:00 CET.
  • Nice to have: basic written German skills.

title: Senior System Architect - Ultrasound (Cambridge, MA or Bothell, WA)
description:
Job Title

Senior System Architect - Ultrasound (Cambridge, MA or Bothell, WA)

Job Description

This role is responsible for setting the direction for the next generation of Philips Ultrasound imaging platforms. As a Senior Systems Architect, you will lead system-level architecture across hardware, software, imaging, transducers, and clinical needs, shaping technology strategy, key product decisions, and future engineering talent.

Your role:

  • Own the long-range architecture vision and technology roadmap for ultrasound imaging platforms, aligning platform strategy with product, portfolio, clinical, and business objectives.
  • Establish architecture principles, platform interfaces, and system-level decision frameworks, translating cross-functional requirements into scalable platform strategies and measurable outcomes.
  • Serve as the technical authority for major programs from concept through launch, governing critical trade-offs across performance, reliability, cost, risk, and architectural integrity.
  • Set the technology agenda for emerging capabilities and future platforms, directing modeling, prototyping, integration, verification, validation, and risk-reduction strategies to enable evidence-based decisions.
  • Provide organizational and technical leadership across product generations, influencing senior leaders, suppliers, and technology partners while mentoring architects and senior engineers and strengthening systems-thinking capabilities.

You're the right fit if:

  • You have a Master’s Degree in a related discipline; PhD preferred.
  • You've acquired 10+ years of industry and/or academic experience in Ultrasound System Architecture, System Design, Hardware Engineering, or equivalent, including significant time as lead architect or technical authority on complex products.
  • You have a track record of defining platform architectures that shipped and scaled across multiple products or generations. You've made high-consequence technology decisions that balance clinical value, risk, quality, cost, and long-term platform strategy.
  • You lead through influence, earning the trust of senior leaders and developing other architects. You bring deep command of design controls and risk management, and you're energized by turning new technology into responsible, differentiated products. You must be able to successfully perform the following minimum Physical, Cognitive and Environmental job requirements with or without accommodation for this position.

How we work together

We believe that we are better together than apart. For our office-based teams, this means working in-person at least 3 days per week. Onsite roles require full-time presence in the company’s facilities. Field roles are most effectively done outside of the company’s main facilities, generally at the customers’ or suppliers’ locations.

This is an office role.

About Philips

We are a health technology company. We built our entire company around the belief that every human matters, and we won't stop until everybody everywhere has access to the quality healthcare that we all deserve. Do the work of your life to help improve the lives of others.

  • Learn more about our business.
  • Discover our rich and exciting history.
  • Learn more about our purpose.
  • Learn more about our culture.

Philips Transparency Details

The pay range for this position in Bothell, WA and Cambridge, MA is $115,000 to $182,000.

The actual base pay offered may vary within the posted ranges depending on multiple factors including job-related knowledge/skills, experience, business needs, geographical location, and internal equity.

In addition, other compensation, such as an annual incentive bonus, sales commission or long-term incentives may be offered. Employees are eligible to participate in our comprehensive Philips Total Rewards benefits program, which includes a generous PTO, 401k (up to 7% match), HSA (with company contribution), stock purchase plan, education reimbursement and much more. Details about our benefits can be found here.

As the North America Sales & Operations Execution (S&OE) Leader, you will lead the hands-on execution of supply chain plans across North America, partnering with key stakeholders to translate plans into action, manage priorities and risks, and drive operational excellence across the end-to-end supply chain.

title: Laboratory Specimen Processor – 3rd Shift
description:
As a Laboratory Specimen Processor at IDEXX, you will help to sort, tag, and prepare the samples for testing. The samples that we work with are blood, urine, fecal samples, and biopsies that we receive from the vet clinics (no animals on-site!) Every sample you help to move along quickly and accurately in the process means we are one step closer to finding out how or why they might be sick. Thanks to you, someone's very beloved pet will get the treatment plan they need - how great is that?

We offer extensive training for this role so whether you’ve worked in a lab before or this would be your first lab job, we hope you’ll consider applying and discover the good you can do on our team.

Please note: The start date for these roles will be between December 15 and December 31st 2026. Please read on for information about these positions! This is a full-time position with excellent day-one benefits.

Why this role matters:

IDEXX reference laboratories is a global network united by a shared commitment to enhancing pet care, where the true strength in our name is the people behind it, including this role. Our reference laboratories make it possible for our customers to discover more with our unrelenting commitment to innovation, personalized support, guidance, and expertise, while providing the most complete and advanced menu of diagnostic tests along with technology and tools. The focus on enhancing the lives of people and pets starts with our own employees and empowering them to achieve their goals, focusing on continuous improvement, and supporting the strong collaboration and inclusiveness that exist in our team.

If you’d like more information about laboratory jobs at IDEXX before applying, you can explore our laboratory careers web page: .


What you’ll be doing as a Laboratory Specimen Processor:

  • You will receive, prepare, and accession veterinary samples (blood, urine, feces, and biopsies) for laboratory analysis and testing.
  • You can expect to remove specimens from transport bags and enter specimen data into a computer tracking system.
  • You will rack and bundle prepared samples for delivery to each testing department.
  • You will assist other lab personnel with specimen storage and ensuring that Turnaround Times (TAT's) are met.


What you’ll need to succeed:

  • You possess a High School diploma or equivalent; a combination of education and experience is required.
  • While not required, previous experience as a specimen accessioner or specimen processor is a nice-to-have.
  • You are someone who thrives in a fast-paced, high-volume work environment.
  • You have a positive attitude and love to bring that energy into the lab every day to support your colleagues.
  • You are looking forward to working in a team.
  • You are able to read, understand, and follow Standard Operating Procedures (SOP’s), including safety and quality procedures.
  • You concentrate on the details and can work reliably and precisely.
  • You have a great sense of team spirit and responsibility.
  • Able to meet the physical requirements that go with working in a lab – standing and sitting for extended periods of time, phone & computer use, extended reach, lifting up to 50lb, and specific vision ability – close, color, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
  • This is a laboratory, so there is potential exposure to biohazards, agents known to cause zoonotic diseases, and hazardous chemicals.


What you can expect from us:

  • Hourly rate: $22.50/hr
  • Opportunity for annual cash bonus and merit pay increase consideration
  • Health / Dental / Vision benefits from day one
  • 5% matching 401k
  • On-the-job training and career advancement opportunities
  • Additional benefits including but not limited to financial support, pet insurance, mental health resources, volunteer paid days off, employee stock program, foundation donation matching, and more
  • The opportunity to do meaningful work where you positively impact the lives of people and pets all over the world


Schedule:

  • This is a full-time (40 hour/week), night-shift position, and we are hiring for the following shifts and schedules:
    • Monday - Friday 11:00 PM - 7:30 AM
    • Sunday - Thursday 11:00 PM - 7:30 AM
  • The shifts and hours may vary depending on business needs
  • Reliable and dependable attendance is an essential function of the position
  • Adherence to attendance-related policies and expectations is critical to this position


Why IDEXX?
We’re proud of the work we do, because our work matters. An innovation leader in every industry we serve since 1983, our team members help pet owners worldwide keep their companion animals healthy and happy, ensure safe drinking water for billions, and help farmers protect livestock and poultry from disease.

We have customers in over 175 countries and a collaborative global workforce. Our culture is one that embraces challenges and encourages learning and discovery. At IDEXX, you’ll be supported by competitive compensation, incentives, and benefits while enjoying purposeful work that drives improvement.

Knowing our work makes a meaningful impact on the health and well-being of pets and people is what motivates us every day. If meaningful work and a sense of purpose are at the top of your list, you’ll find it here.

Let’s pursue what matters together.

IDEXX values a diverse workforce and workplace and strongly encourages women, people of color, LGBTQ+ individuals, people with disabilities, members of ethnic minorities, foreign-born residents, and veterans to apply. IDEXX is an equal opportunity employer. Applicants will not be discriminated against because of race, color, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, citizenship status, disability, ancestry, marital status, veteran status, medical condition, or any protected category prohibited by local, state, or federal laws.

Applicants must be authorized to work for ANY employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa for this role.

This role is responsible for ensuring successful adoption of industry-specific AI solutions by translating customer requirements into configured, deployed, and production-ready implementations.

The ideal candidate combines product implementation expertise, customer-facing consulting skills, and strong technical capabilities across cloud, AI, and platform technologies within Manufacturing environments. Working closely with customer stakeholders, product teams, solution architects, and engineers, this individual will lead engagements from discovery through production deployment, configuring platform capabilities, integrating customer systems, enabling business users, and driving measurable business outcomes. The FDE serves as a trusted advisor throughout the implementation lifecycle while providing feedback that helps improve product capabilities and accelerate future deployments.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead end-to-end implementation of AI products within customer environments, including discovery, design, configuration, deployment, user adoption, and optimization activities.
  • Partner with customer stakeholders to understand business objectives, operational processes, challenges, and success criteria.
  • Translate customer business requirements, workflows, and operating procedures into platform configurations, business rules, integrations, and AI-enabled workflows.
  • Configure and deploy product capabilities, including workflows, connectors, business rules, extraction models, and customer-specific settings.
  • Collaborate with product, engineering, architecture, and customer teams to ensure implementations align with business requirements and technical standards.
  • Deploy and support AI product solutions within cloud and customer-hosted environments using established deployment and operational processes.
  • Integrate products with customer applications, data sources, APIs, identity platforms, and enterprise systems.
  • Conduct implementation workshops, design reviews, user training sessions, and solution demonstrations with business and technical stakeholders.
  • Monitor implementation performance, troubleshoot issues, and recommend improvements to optimize adoption, scalability, and operational outcomes.
  • Document solution configurations, implementation approaches, deployment procedures, and operational best practices.
  • Provide structured feedback to product and engineering teams regarding customer requirements, enhancement opportunities, recurring implementation patterns, and product improvement recommendations.
  • Contribute reusable assets, implementation playbooks, configuration templates, and deployment methodologies that improve delivery consistency and scalability.

  • 6+ years of experience in software engineering, solution engineering, implementation consulting, platform engineering, DevOps, customer engineering, or a related technology role.
  • 2+ years of experience implementing, configuring, deploying, or supporting enterprise software products, SaaS platforms, AI solutions, or cloud-based applications within Manufacturing customer environments.

  • Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP), application integration, APIs, containerized applications, or deployment automation technologies in a production environment.

title: DevOps Engineer - Jersey City, NJ
description:
Req ID: 383761

NTT DATA strives to hire exceptional, innovative and passionate individuals who want to grow with us. If you want to be part of an inclusive, adaptable, and forward-thinking organization, apply now.

We are currently seeking a DevOps Engineer - Jersey City, NJ to join our team in Jersey City, New Jersey (US-NJ), United States (US).

Join a high-impact DevOps team within a global organization where you'll play a key role in modernizing cloud infrastructure, driving automation, and improving software delivery at scale. This position offers the opportunity to work with cutting-edge cloud, CI/CD, Kubernetes, and Infrastructure as Code technologies while partnering across engineering, security, and operations teams. If you're passionate about solving complex technical challenges, building reliable platforms, and growing your career in a collaborative environment with long-term advancement opportunities, we'd love to hear from you.

Roles and Responsibilities:
- Design, implement, and maintain CI/CD pipelines to automate application build, testing, deployment, and release processes using Jenkins/GitHub/DevSecOps functions.
- Develop and manage Infrastructure as Code (IaC) solutions using tools such as Terraform, CloudFormation, or Ansible.
- Administer and support cloud platforms (AWS or Azure) to ensure scalable, secure, and highly available environments.
- Create and maintain docker files, manifest files, and HELM Charts for different environments\orchestrators.
- Automate infrastructure provisioning, configuration management, and deployment activities.
- Collaborate with development, QA, security, and operations teams to streamline software delivery and deployment processes.
- Implement and maintain automated testing frameworks within CI/CD pipelines.
- Ensure high availability, disaster recovery, backup, and business continuity solutions for critical systems.
- Configure and manage web servers, application servers, and middleware components.
- Perform system troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and incident resolution for production environments.
- Establish and enforce DevOps best practices, standards, and operational procedures.

Required Skills
- Demonstrated ability to utilize modern monitoring tools (such as DataDog, Prometheus, or Splunk, …)
- Knowledge of WS Cloud DevOps services such as Jenkins, IAM, VPC, ECS, Lambda, RDS, CloudFormation, or similar technologies
- Knowledge of Docker containers and PaaS (such as Cloud Foundry, Kubernetes, OpenShift, Rancher) highly desired.
- Hands-on Kubernetes skills and knowledge
- Expertise in Production support, including incident management, root cause analysis, real-time monitoring, and high availability and reliability of critical systems in a fast-paced environment.
- Experience engineering/sizing, installing, configuring, and maintaining mission critical applications.
- Hands-on Azure Active Directory experience
- Strong analytical, technical, and problem-solving skills to troubleshoot issues in the cloud.
- Experience in Instrumentation with systems skills on building and operating, monitoring, logging, alerting services of distributed systems at scale
- Demonstrated ability to learn and experiment with new technologies and patterns

Basic Requirements
- 5+ years of hands-on experience with one or more of the languages (such as Python, Java, Go, or Javascript etc.)
- 5+ years of solid experience working with public cloud and cloud infrastructure build
- 3+ years of experience provisioning compute resources or managing IAAM roles and subscriptions in the cloud
- 3 + years of experience building VPCs, private networks and network routes and rules in the public cloud.
- 3+ years of experience managing systems using infrastructure as code tools (such as CloudFormation, Terraform, or ARM etc..)
- 3+ years of experience building CI-CD pipelines for DevSecOps functions

Preferred Qualifications
- Cloud platform experience with certifications preferred (such as AWS or Azure)
- 3+ years of hands on Experience on Deployments tools like Udeploy, Starling, or Mario

title: Principal Engineer - AI Enablement
description:
Principal Software Engineer - AI Developer Productivity | Belfast | Hybrid

  • £85,000 - £95,000 plus a strong benefits package
  • Principal-level software engineer... lead through influence, not line management
  • Hybrid: 2 days a week in the Belfast office
  • Stack-agnostic: Java, .NET, Python, Go and more
  • Make AI part of everyday engineering for a global organisation
  • Exclusive to Ocho People... not advertised anywhere else

About the Company

Our client is a global financial technology leader whose platforms quietly power everyday life for millions of businesses in more than 175 countries. A major acquisition this year has more than doubled the size of the business, and it is putting over a billion dollars a year into innovation. Belfast is one of its most important engineering hubs, home to teams building systems that the world simply expects to work.

The Role

Think about the best engineer you've worked with who got everyone else excited about AI. The one who built the tool, shared the workflow and showed the team it actually works. That's who this role is for.

This is a software engineering role first. You'll take the best of what's happening in AI across the organisation, from communities and innovation days to experiments in shared repos, and turn it into practical tools that engineers use every day. You'll work across multiple teams in Belfast and the US, backed by senior leadership who are serious about making engineers faster and happier, not about replacing them.

You'll have the freedom to experiment, the trust to make calls, and the scale to see your work make a real difference.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build AI skills, agents and workflows that teams can pick up and use straight away
  • Decide which AI tools and practices are worth scaling and which are just noise
  • Bring AI into CI/CD, testing and release processes safely and with care
  • Lead small tiger teams with architects, product managers and subject matter experts to solve real problems
  • Measure the impact with clear baseline efficiency metrics
  • Set standards for secure, responsible AI use in a highly regulated environment
  • Coach and mentor engineers so AI-first working becomes the norm
  • Turn ambitious ideas from senior leaders into plans that actually ship

What You'll Need

Essential:

  • 10-15 years as a hands-on software engineer, and still close to the code
  • Proof you have driven AI adoption in a real engineering team, not just used the tools yourself
  • Strong working knowledge of tools and ideas like Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, agents, MCP and context engineering
  • A full view of the SDLC, from design through to CI/CD and production
  • A careful, quality-first approach... you know when to slow down
  • The confidence to explain and influence at every level, from engineers to directors
  • Based in Northern Ireland and able to be in Belfast 2 days a week

Desirable:

  • Financial services or other regulated industry experience
  • Experience setting up developer productivity or DORA metrics
  • Hands-on work with LLM frameworks or evaluation tooling

Please note: this is a software engineering leadership role, so it is not suited to data science or ML research profiles.

Why Apply?

  • £85,000 - £95,000 plus a strong benefits package
  • Hybrid working with only 2 days a week in Belfast
  • A rare chance to shape how a global engineering organisation uses AI
  • Real backing from senior leadership who want change, not another pilot
  • Access to Copilot and multiple LLMs, with room to experiment
  • Your work will reach platforms used by millions of businesses
  • A quick, simple process with no coding test
  • They want to move fast, so you could start within weeks

Next Steps

If you're the engineer who gets everyone else excited about AI, let's talk. Connect with Chanel Gillen on LinkedIn or email for a confidential chat.

title: Integral Project Leader
description:
Job Title

Integral Project Leader

Job Description

You are responsible for

  • Give direction and leads complex, integral projects, from initial phase until introduction in the Market or until internal company delivery, which are essential to Philips organizational strategy involving multiple business domains and knowledge centers inside and outside Philips and/or external business partners and/or customers.
  • Set strategic direction within the project(s) and related projects / program
  • Articulate complex schedules and interdependencies in a consumable way for stakeholders, can identify risks and issues and identifies mitigation actions and understands when to escalate.
  • In collaboration with project stakeholders identifies project risks (opportunities and threats) and issues, identify mitigation actions and supports in fostering a risk environment where considerate risk-taking behavior is encouraged, taking into consideration the balance between risk taking and risk escalations.
  • Apply daily management and methodical problem solving, partners with key stakeholders to constantly search for creative and innovative ways to elevate the capabilities of the portfolio and maintains advanced knowledge of business lines and products/services, as well as the competitive market.
  • Recognize critical project knowledge, value lessons learned, and share critical project knowledge in the Philips Knowledge Hub. Drive opportunities in the Philips PM community to add value and uses internal network to advance other teams.
  • Deliver innovative solutions that improve single domain business activities and/or operations and impact the long-term goals in the organization.
  • Responsible for project goals and objectives, key process decisions and alignment with project stakeholders related to large projects.
  • KPIs projections, tracking, and reporting for assigned initiatives.
  • Report project status regularly to key stakeholders and obtaining stakeholders’ approvals for completing each key milestone and major plan changes with discipline.
  • Deliver the quality initiatives via project and product development execution.
  • Support continuous improvement and compliance processes and initiatives according to corporate policies and procedures
  • Manage Change Management procedures as appropriate.
  • Maintain awareness of new and emerging technologies and the potential application on relevant G&B Product Development
  • The position requires a high degree of flexibility and the ability to work both independently and within a team. Excellent problem solving, critical thinking, analytical and communication skills are necessary to successfully deliver Philips G&B products and present Philips G&B message to individuals and groups in a professional manner.



To succeed in this role, you should have the following skills and experience

Essential:

  • Bachelor/master’s degree in a relevant discipline (e.g. business or engineering preferred)
  • 8+ years in engineering/R&D project management successfully leading large complex programs, projects, and initiatives with structured approach (e.g., PMP, Prince2, Agile)
  • Subject Matter Expert in all aspects of Project Management plan-driven methodology, including Governance, Monitoring & Controlling, Scope Management, Schedule Management, Financial Management, Issue & Risk Management, Vendor, Contract, & Resources Management
  • Good technical knowledge and understanding of electronics and mechanical design aspects of household or consumer products.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills while maintaining high-quality standards.
  • Ability to tailor information and pitch at differing levels of detail, especially presenting management information to assist with and enable decision making.
  • Strong leadership and stakeholder management skills to drive change & standardization across the businesses and markets.
  • Strong interpersonal skills, result oriented self-starter with excellent communication and people skills, attention to detail and initiative.
  • Fluent in English and Chinese Languages
  • Willing to travel.



How we work together
We believe that we are better together than apart. For our office-based teams, this means working in-person at least 4 days per week. Onsite roles require full-time presence in the company’s facilities. Field roles are most effectively done outside of the company’s main facilities, generally at the customers’ or suppliers’ locations.

If you’re interested in this role and have many, but not all, of the experiences needed, we encourage you to apply. You may still be the right candidate for this or other opportunities at Philips. Learn more about our culture of impact with care.

title: System Integration Test Engineer - Automotive-based in Craiova
description:
Who We Are

We don’t just develop embedded software — we engineer intelligence into products. The Embedded Competence Center at NTT DATA Romania brings together experts in embedded systems, firmware development, and hardware–software integration, delivering robust and high-performance solutions for complex, safety-critical environments. With strong expertise in C/C++, AUTOSAR, real-time operating systems, and communication protocols, we design scalable embedded architectures, integrate software seamlessly with hardware, and ensure compliance with industry standards. Across the industries we support — from Automotive and Industrial Automation to Smart Devices and IoT — we transform reliable embedded technology into a foundation for innovative, dependable products.

As a System Integration Test Engineer, you will be responsible for the integration, testing and validation of complex embedded automotive systems. You will work closely with System Engineering, Software Development and Integration teams, translating system requirements and architecture into effective test scenarios, executing tests on HIL environments and contributing to test automation.

The role requires previous hands-on experience in embedded systems testing, system integration or automotive validation, ideally with dSPACE, IBM Rhapsody and automotive communication protocols.

Location: Craiova, Romania – minimum 80% on-site (requiered)

What you'll be doing

  • Analyze and understand system requirements, system architecture and functional models, including models defined in IBM Rhapsody.
  • Derive test specifications, test scenarios and test cases based on system requirements and architecture.
  • Develop and maintain automated test cases using dSPACE AutomationDesk.
  • Execute and monitor tests using dSPACE AutomationDesk / ControlDesk and HIL environments.
  • Perform automated, manual and exploratory testing, including basic vehicle-level checks such as smoke tests.
  • Analyze system behavior and identify appropriate test boundaries, interfaces and coverage.
  • Analyze test results, investigate deviations and report defects using ALM and requirements management tools such as DOORS NextGen and EWM.
  • Set up, configure and maintain HIL test environments, including HW/SW simulations.
  • Connect and configure ECUs, restbus simulations, measurement devices and test benches.
  • Perform measurements and collect technical evidence using oscilloscopes, signal traces, logs and other instrumentation.
  • Support root-cause analysis by correlating test results, communication signals and system behavior.
  • Collaborate within Agile development teams, providing testing input during sprint planning, reviews and other development activities.
  • Work closely with internal and external project teams to ensure efficient integration and high-quality delivery.
  • Provide on-site testing and integration support when required.
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of testing processes, test coverage and automation.

What you'll bring along

  • Previous professional experience in System Testing, System Integration, Verification & Validation or Embedded Software Testing, preferably within the automotive industry.
  • Good understanding of electronics, embedded systems and automotive ECUs.
  • Hands-on experience with HIL testing and system-level validation.
  • Experience with dSPACE AutomationDesk and/or ControlDesk is highly desirable.
  • Experience with IBM Rhapsody, system modeling and interpretation of system architecture diagrams is considered a strong advantage.
  • Good understanding of automotive communication protocols such as CAN, LIN, Automotive Ethernet and/or FlexRay.
  • Experience with test and measurement equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters and power supplies.
  • Programming or scripting experience with Python, C and/or C++.
  • Experience with requirements management and ALM tools, preferably DOORS NextGen and EWM.
  • Ability to understand system requirements and translate them into structured and traceable test cases.
  • Experience working in Agile development environments.
  • ISTQB certification is considered an advantage.
  • Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, with a structured approach to identifying and investigating system-level issues.
  • Proactive and solution-oriented mindset, with an interest in continuously improving testing processes and automation.
  • Good communication and collaboration skills.
  • Good command of English.

title: Pharmacy Intern - Grad
description:
You’ve invested a lot of time and energy in your education. Now you want the chance to make your mark. We offer challenging opportunities for you to learn and grow professionally. In our programs, you’ll be immersed in a culture of continuous improvement, with the goal of changing health care for the better.

Position Summary:

At CVS Health, we are focused on transforming health care for our customers and making our company a great place to work. We help people navigate the health care system – and their personal health care – by improving access, lowering costs and being a trusted partner for every meaningful moment of health. Within our Retail locations, we bring this promise to life with heart every day and our Graduate Pharmacy Interns play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise, while developing their own skills in preparation for increasing responsibility.

As a Graduate Pharmacy Intern, you will apply your didactic learning from pharmacy school and pharmacy practice into real-world practice to become ready for a Pharmacist role. Under the direction of your preceptor and District Leader, you will complete a comprehensive training roadmap within 120 days of graduation designed to further your knowledge of store, district, and regional operations. Through your hands-on experience, training roadmap, and time spent with leaders in your district you will deepen your understanding of patient safety and error prevention, quality assurance drug utilization review (DUR), pharmacy professional standards such as corresponding responsibility and red flag detection. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate empathy and genuine care, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.

As tenure and readiness increase, you will take on greater accountability for supporting the management, oversight, and operations within the pharmacy, including but not limited to:

  • Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health
  • Following pharmacy workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment
  • Contributing to positive patient experiences by showing empathy and genuine care: creating heartfelt and personalized moments while serving patients at pick-up, drive-thru, and over the phone; keeping patients healthy by offering immunizations and other services at the register and over the phone; and demonstrating compassionate care by solving or escalating patient problems
  • Offering to counsel, fielding medical questions, and soliciting information on a patient’s medical history to provide optimal care, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist
  • Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation
  • Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices
  • Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.
  • Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients
  • Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business
  • Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. Complying with CVS policies and procedures to ensure patient safety, compliance with controlled substance dispensing and recordkeeping, and to protect patient privacy and security
  • Delivering additional patient health care services (e.g., immunizations, point-of-care testing, and voluntarily staffing offsite clinics), where allowable by law and supported by required training and certification

Where permissible, the Graduate Pharmacy Intern may also support immunizations, which includes the following responsibilities:

  • Completing additional licensure and training requirements, in compliance with state Board of Pharmacy regulations, to obtain Technician Immunizer status to support preparing and administering vaccines
  • Educating patients about vaccines and answering questions to obtain informed consent
  • Monitoring for, and responding to, adverse reactions; reporting adverse reaction events per public health requirements
  • Reviewing and collecting patient information; tracking and documenting for each applicable patient

Required Qualifications:

  • PharmD graduate of a U.S. accredited program prior to beginning the Post-Graduate Training Program at CVS Health
  • Ability to obtain required pharmacist licensure within the required timeframe, per state guidelines. Failure to obtain required Pharmacist licensure within 120 days of graduation will result in separation of employment.
  • Must possess, or be in the process of obtaining, valid intern and/or technician licensure as required

Essential Functions:

  • Regular and predictable attendance, including nights and weekends
  • Ability to complete required training within designated timeframe
  • Attention and Focus:
    • Ability to concentrate on a task over a period of time
    • Ability to pivot quickly from one task to another to meet patient and business needs
    • Ability to confirm prescription information and label accuracy, ensuring patient safety
  • Customer Service and Team Orientation:
    • Actively look for ways to help people, and do so in a friendly manner
    • Notice and understand patients’ reactions, and respond appropriately
  • Communication Skills:
    • Use and understand verbal and written communication to interact with patients and colleagues
    • Utilize active listening by giving full attention to what others are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times
  • Mathematical Reasoning:
    • Ability to use math to solve a problem, such as determining the total number of tablets to dispense, day’s supply, and/or number of full bottles and additional bottles needed to fill a prescription
  • Problem Resolution:
    • Identifying challenging patient or colleague interactions and choosing the best course of action when faced multiple options
  • Physical Demands:
    • Be mobile and remain upright for extended periods of time
    • Lift, scan, and bag items
    • Reach overhead; stretch or reach out with the body, arms, and/or legs to grasp items
    • Move fingers repetitively; picking, pinching, typing, or otherwise working primarily with fingers rather than whole hand or arm
    • Extend hand(s) and arm(s) multiple directions to place, move, or lift items
    • Control precision; quickly adjust machines to exact positions
    • Stoop to a considerable degree, requiring full use of the lower extremities and back muscles to move items between low and high positions, including bending spine at the waist
    • Close visual acuity to perform activities such as: transcribing, viewing a computer terminal, reading, visual inspection involving small parts
    • Occasionally lift of up to 20 lbs and/or exert up to 20 lbs. of force; Frequently lift of up to 10 lbs and/or exert up to 10 lbs. of force; Consistently lift and/or exert a negligible amount of force to move objects.
    • Express or exchange ideas by means of spoken word where detailed or important spoken instructions must be conveyed accurately
    • Have the ability to receive detailed information through oral communication
  • Any additional tasks as directed by Supervisor or Manager

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 1+ years of related work experience in pharmacy, retail, medical, or customer service setting
  • Ability to become immunization certified: Once state regulations are met, pharmacy interns should be striving to provide patient immunizations as this is an essential pharmacist function
  • Ability to work in home store, and across the market in other locations, to meet business needs
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Suite (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, etc.)

Pay Range

$24.25 - $42.00


Whether in our pharmacies or through our health service offerings, we are pioneering a bold new approach to total health care. As health care innovators, we are making quality care affordable, accessible, simple and seamless. We await your fresh ideas, new perspectives, and the unique contributions you will make to our organization.

title: Pharmacy Intern - Grad
description:
You’ve invested a lot of time and energy in your education. Now you want the chance to make your mark. We offer challenging opportunities for you to learn and grow professionally. In our programs, you’ll be immersed in a culture of continuous improvement, with the goal of changing health care for the better.

Position Summary:

At CVS Health, we are focused on transforming health care for our customers and making our company a great place to work. We help people navigate the health care system – and their personal health care – by improving access, lowering costs and being a trusted partner for every meaningful moment of health. Within our Retail locations, we bring this promise to life with heart every day and our Graduate Pharmacy Interns play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise, while developing their own skills in preparation for increasing responsibility.

As a Graduate Pharmacy Intern, you will apply your didactic learning from pharmacy school and pharmacy practice into real-world practice to become ready for a Pharmacist role. Under the direction of your preceptor and District Leader, you will complete a comprehensive training roadmap within 120 days of graduation designed to further your knowledge of store, district, and regional operations. Through your hands-on experience, training roadmap, and time spent with leaders in your district you will deepen your understanding of patient safety and error prevention, quality assurance drug utilization review (DUR), pharmacy professional standards such as corresponding responsibility and red flag detection. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate empathy and genuine care, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.

As tenure and readiness increase, you will take on greater accountability for supporting the management, oversight, and operations within the pharmacy, including but not limited to:

  • Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health
  • Following pharmacy workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment
  • Contributing to positive patient experiences by showing empathy and genuine care: creating heartfelt and personalized moments while serving patients at pick-up, drive-thru, and over the phone; keeping patients healthy by offering immunizations and other services at the register and over the phone; and demonstrating compassionate care by solving or escalating patient problems
  • Offering to counsel, fielding medical questions, and soliciting information on a patient’s medical history to provide optimal care, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist
  • Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation
  • Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices
  • Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.
  • Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients
  • Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business
  • Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. Complying with CVS policies and procedures to ensure patient safety, compliance with controlled substance dispensing and recordkeeping, and to protect patient privacy and security
  • Delivering additional patient health care services (e.g., immunizations, point-of-care testing, and voluntarily staffing offsite clinics), where allowable by law and supported by required training and certification

Where permissible, the Graduate Pharmacy Intern may also support immunizations, which includes the following responsibilities:

  • Completing additional licensure and training requirements, in compliance with state Board of Pharmacy regulations, to obtain Technician Immunizer status to support preparing and administering vaccines
  • Educating patients about vaccines and answering questions to obtain informed consent
  • Monitoring for, and responding to, adverse reactions; reporting adverse reaction events per public health requirements
  • Reviewing and collecting patient information; tracking and documenting for each applicable patient

Required Qualifications:

  • PharmD graduate of a U.S. accredited program prior to beginning the Post-Graduate Training Program at CVS Health
  • Ability to obtain required pharmacist licensure within the required timeframe, per state guidelines. Failure to obtain required Pharmacist licensure within 120 days of graduation will result in separation of employment.
  • Must possess, or be in the process of obtaining, valid intern and/or technician licensure as required

Essential Functions:

  • Regular and predictable attendance, including nights and weekends
  • Ability to complete required training within designated timeframe
  • Attention and Focus:
    • Ability to concentrate on a task over a period of time
    • Ability to pivot quickly from one task to another to meet patient and business needs
    • Ability to confirm prescription information and label accuracy, ensuring patient safety
  • Customer Service and Team Orientation:
    • Actively look for ways to help people, and do so in a friendly manner
    • Notice and understand patients’ reactions, and respond appropriately
  • Communication Skills:
    • Use and understand verbal and written communication to interact with patients and colleagues
    • Utilize active listening by giving full attention to what others are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times
  • Mathematical Reasoning:
    • Ability to use math to solve a problem, such as determining the total number of tablets to dispense, day’s supply, and/or number of full bottles and additional bottles needed to fill a prescription
  • Problem Resolution:
    • Identifying challenging patient or colleague interactions and choosing the best course of action when faced multiple options
  • Physical Demands:
    • Be mobile and remain upright for extended periods of time
    • Lift, scan, and bag items
    • Reach overhead; stretch or reach out with the body, arms, and/or legs to grasp items
    • Move fingers repetitively; picking, pinching, typing, or otherwise working primarily with fingers rather than whole hand or arm
    • Extend hand(s) and arm(s) multiple directions to place, move, or lift items
    • Control precision; quickly adjust machines to exact positions
    • Stoop to a considerable degree, requiring full use of the lower extremities and back muscles to move items between low and high positions, including bending spine at the waist
    • Close visual acuity to perform activities such as: transcribing, viewing a computer terminal, reading, visual inspection involving small parts
    • Occasionally lift of up to 20 lbs and/or exert up to 20 lbs. of force; Frequently lift of up to 10 lbs and/or exert up to 10 lbs. of force; Consistently lift and/or exert a negligible amount of force to move objects.
    • Express or exchange ideas by means of spoken word where detailed or important spoken instructions must be conveyed accurately
    • Have the ability to receive detailed information through oral communication
  • Any additional tasks as directed by Supervisor or Manager

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 1+ years of related work experience in pharmacy, retail, medical, or customer service setting
  • Ability to become immunization certified: Once state regulations are met, pharmacy interns should be striving to provide patient immunizations as this is an essential pharmacist function
  • Ability to work in home store, and across the market in other locations, to meet business needs
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Suite (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, etc.)

Pay Range

The typical pay range for this role is:


$23.75 - $42.00


Whether in our pharmacies or through our health service offerings, we are pioneering a bold new approach to total health care. As health care innovators, we are making quality care affordable, accessible, simple and seamless. We await your fresh ideas, new perspectives, and the unique contributions you will make to our organization.

Great benefits for great people

We take pride in offering a comprehensive and competitive mix of pay and benefits that reflects our commitment to our colleagues and their families.

This part‑time position is eligible for a range of benefits and programs that support the physical, emotional, and financial well‑being of colleagues. title: Part time Post-Doctoral Research Assistant - Sustainable Fashion and Behaviour Change (Fixed Term)
description:
What helps people repair, reuse and care for their clothes, and what gets in the way? Join Bath Spa University’s Future Fashion Works to research how community hubs can make sustainable fashion more accessible through Restitch the Future, a four-year programme delivered with A Single Thread CIC and supported by The National Lottery Community Fund’s Climate Action Fund.
This is a part time role, with a working pattern of 22.2 hours per week (0.6 FTE).

  • Develop and deliver a focused research and evaluation programme with Future Fashion Works, A Single Thread CIC and participating community hubs.
  • Design and carry out research into clothing consumption, repair and reuse, using appropriate qualitative, quantitative and participatory methods.
  • Establish baselines and track change across selected hubs, exploring what supports lasting behaviour change and how to reach people who have not previously taken part.
  • Investigate barriers to participation and work with the project’s EDI Advisory Board and delivery partners to make research and feedback accessible to underrepresented communities.
  • Develop practical research tools, support hub partners with data collection and analyse the findings. Secure ethical approvals and follow University requirements for consent, safeguarding and data protection.
  • Use the findings to inform the national community engagement strategy and practical playbook for sustainable fashion hubs. Contribute evidence to funder reports and produce peer-reviewed publications, conference contributions and accessible outputs for practitioners and communities.
  • A completed PhD or equivalent doctoral-level research experience in a relevant discipline, with evidence of high-quality research outputs appropriate to career stage.
  • Experience of designing and delivering research relevant to sustainable fashion, consumption, behaviour change, communities, sustainability or climate action.
  • Experience of working with communities or external partners, building trust and adapting research methods to different participants and settings.
  • Ability to select appropriate qualitative and/or quantitative methods, analyse evidence and explain its limitations, with knowledge of research ethics and responsible data management.
  • Ability to plan and prioritise a focused research programme, meet agreed deadlines and communicate findings clearly to academic, practitioner and community audiences.

title: PLANNING MANAGER
description:
Summary Description of Position

The Planning Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, strategic direction, and performance of the Planning Department. This position oversees maintenance planning, production support, conversion planning, and departmental resource management to ensure maintenance events are effectively planned, coordinated, and executed.

Develops and oversees short-term and long-range forecasts for manpower, materials, facilities, and other resources required to support current and anticipated maintenance events. Works closely with Operations, Production, Materials, Engineering, Quality, customers, and corporate leadership to ensure planning objectives align with operational demands, customer commitments, and company goals.

Provides direct leadership and oversight to the Planning Supervisor and Production Support Supervisor while establishing departmental priorities, monitoring performance metrics, managing budgets, and driving continuous improvement initiatives.

Benefits

  • Generous Paid Time Off (PTO)

  • Paid company holidays

  • 401(k) retirement plan with 5% company match

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • Company-paid life insurance

  • Short- and long-term disability coverage

  • Ongoing training and professional development opportunities

Minimum Requirements and Qualifications

  • Seven (7) or more years of related experience in aircraft maintenance planning, production control, or heavy maintenance operations.

  • Five (5) or more years in supervisory or management capacities of increasing responsibility, or demonstrated ability to perform the duties and responsibilities of the position.

  • Broad working knowledge of aircraft maintenance, aircraft modifications, maintenance planning processes and procedures, and production control operations.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead, develop, and manage multiple teams and supervisory personnel.

  • Strong understanding of manpower planning, labor forecasting, material requirements, maintenance scheduling, and resource allocation.

  • Experience developing and managing departmental budgets, operational forecasts, and performance metrics.

  • Excellent written, verbal, presentation, organizational, and interpersonal communication skills.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly advanced Excel, and other applicable planning and reporting software.

  • Working knowledge of FAA regulations and Federal Aviation Regulations pertaining to FAR Part 145 repair station operations.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Aviation Management, Aviation Technology, Business Administration, or a related field.

  • Previous management experience within a heavy aircraft maintenance MRO environment.

  • Experience developing maintenance program quotes, proposals, and customer bid submissions.

  • Working knowledge of maintenance planning systems, including Wings.

  • Knowledge of process improvement methodologies such as Lean Principles and Six Sigma.

Major Responsibility Areas and Duties

  • Provides overall leadership, direction, and accountability for all facets of the Planning Department, including maintenance planning, production support, and conversion planning.

  • Directly manages and provides oversight to the Planning Supervisor and Production Support Supervisor, establishing departmental objectives, priorities, and performance expectations.

  • Oversees the development and execution of short-term and long-range maintenance plans, ensuring manpower, material, facility, and equipment requirements are identified and coordinated in advance of maintenance events.

  • Ensures detailed maintenance work scopes, labor estimates, material requirements, and production schedules are developed to support operational readiness and customer commitments.

  • Coordinates with Operations, Production, Materials, Engineering, Quality, and other departments to address planning constraints and maintain alignment with maintenance schedules.

  • Develops, manages, and monitors the annual Planning Department budget, evaluating expenditures, staffing requirements, and resource utilization.

  • Reviews Aircraft Task Orders (ATO) prior to bid submission to ensure planning requirements, labor estimates, and associated resources are appropriately evaluated.

  • Serves as a primary point of contact for customers and corporate marketing regarding maintenance planning, scheduling, and related operational requirements.

  • Oversees the preparation, maintenance, and distribution of operational status reports, including the Hangar Load Plan.

  • Establishes and monitors departmental business metrics to evaluate productivity, efficiency, and overall planning effectiveness.

  • Analyzes operational performance and identifies opportunities to improve maintenance flow, resource utilization, and departmental processes.

  • Ensures effective communication between departmental leadership, employees, customers, and corporate stakeholders.

Additional Duties

  • Performs other duties as assigned by immediate supervisor.

Physical Requirements and Environmental Conditions

  • Ability to perform work utilizing a computer for extended periods of time.

  • Ability to sit for extended periods in a normal office environment.

  • Ability to withstand constant to intermittent loud noise levels.

  • Ability to have correctable near and far vision.

  • Ability to have distance vision.

title: Principal AI Engineer (Forward Deployed)
description:
Principal AI Engineer (Forward Deployed)

At-a-Glance
- Principal-level individual contributor role embedded directly with customers
- Building AI capability against live operational problems, at pace
- Python, large language models, agentic workflows, data integration
- Set the technical standard for how AI gets deployed across every customer
- Share options and an unusually short distance between idea and impact

About the Company
My client is a UK technology company building an AI operating and orchestration layer that puts intelligent systems to work inside large, complex organisations where accuracy and accountability really matter. The platform is already live and in daily operational use with major customers. The engineering group is small, senior and unusually fast moving, with AI tooling built into how the team genuinely works rather than bolted on afterwards.

The Role
This is a forward deployed role in the truest sense. You go to where the problem is, work alongside the people who have it, and build against it in days rather than quarters. At principal level you are also the technical authority for how that work gets done, setting the patterns, calling the hard architectural questions, and lifting the engineers around you. It suits a very experienced engineer who wants real influence without moving into people management, and who is motivated by problems that matter rather than problems that scale neatly.

Key Responsibilities
- Embed with customer teams to understand operational problems first hand
- Build working AI solutions rapidly against real data and real constraints
- Set the technical approach and architectural patterns used across deployments
- Own the hardest problems, the ones nobody else has managed to crack
- Design and tune retrieval, prompting and agent behaviour for demanding use cases
- Establish the standard for how output quality is validated before it is relied upon
- Convert successful deployments into repeatable product capability
- Mentor senior engineers and act as the technical voice with senior customer stakeholders

What You'll Need

Essential:
- 8+ years building software or AI systems in production
- Deep Python expertise and substantial hands-on large language model experience
- Track record of shipping quickly in ambiguous, under-specified situations
- Experience setting technical direction that other engineers then follow
- Confident working directly with customers, including in operational settings
- Eligible for UK security clearance

Desirable / Nice to Have:
- Previous forward deployed, field engineering or embedded consulting experience
- Background delivering into a heavily regulated or operationally critical domain
- Open source contribution, patents or published technical work

Why Apply?
- The shortest possible distance between a real problem and a working solution
- Genuine principal-level scope, not a senior role with a better title
- Share options as part of the package
- Almost no bureaucracy between you and shipping
- Flexible working pattern
- Direct line to founders and senior leadership
- Shape how an entire engineering function operates while it is still being built

Benefits:
